card: Changes CWallet::CommitTransaction and interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction to return broadcast errors via util::Expected instead of returning void. This fixes an issue where the QML GUI reports 'Transaction sent' even when the node rejects the transaction (bitcoin-core/gui-qml#1008). Existing wallet RPC and Qt widget callers ignore the return value to prevent unintended behavioral changes.

enables: bitcoin-core/gui-qml PR consuming the error to report rejection
Follow-up PR propagating errors in commitBumpTransaction

evidence: PR description: 'The QML GUI shows "Transaction sent" even when the node rejected the transaction, because CWallet::CommitTransaction() only logs the rejection and returns void' (addressing bitcoin-core/gui-qml#1008).
problem: CWallet::CommitTransaction discarded broadcast failures and returned void after logging. Frontends such as the QML GUI could not detect whether the node accepted or rejected the transaction, causing them to display misleading 'Transaction sent' confirmations even on rejection.

risk.why: A mistake in transaction commitment or error propagation could disrupt transaction broadcast or corrupt wallet interface state.

scope_notes: Touches wallet interface definitions and broadcast helpers across wallet and node boundaries, though callers are updated to preserve legacy behavior.
summary: Changes CWallet::CommitTransaction and interfaces::Wallet::commitTransaction to return a util::Expected<void, TransactionBroadcastError> instead of void. It introduces TransactionBroadcastError pairing a TransactionError code with an error message, and adds a SUBMISSION_SKIPPED error code for transactions bypassed before submission. Existing callers such as RPCs and the Qt widget interface ignore the new return value to preserve existing behavior.
